target_customer: Urban consumers in Lagos and Abuja ordering chef-prepared meals via app
problem: Aggregator food delivery in Africa gives inconsistent quality and cost control; FoodCourt cooks under its own virtual brands to control the full chain.
business_model: Full-stack virtual restaurants and dark kitchens selling directly to consumers via its app (legal entity Co-Kitchen Workspace Limited)
product_category: Cloud kitchen and virtual restaurant operator

founders.name: Henry Nneji
previous_startups: Fashion Map, co-founded 2019, described by The Economist as Uber for Tailors
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: background in design, marketing, product management and entrepreneurship

founders.name: Paul Adokiye Iruene
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: full-stack engineer across backend, web, mobile, AI/ML and DevOps

exit.reason: TechCabal reports FoodCourt paused operations in 2026 after unpaid salaries and vendor debts while awaiting a funding facility that did not arrive; the co-founder says it intends to relaunch after restructuring

competitors.name: Jumia Food
competitors.traction_then: orders grew 30 percent month on month during lockdowns in Lagos (reported)

competitors.name: Bolt Food
competitors.what: Ride-hailing company's food delivery launched in Nigeria (official launch October 2021)

competitors.name: Gokada
competitors.what: Bike courier platform that switched to food delivery

technical_complexity.rationale: Consumer ordering app and kitchen operations; the difficulty is operational execution rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Owned virtual brands and kitchens give control but little structural moat; margins depend on operations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Jumia Food and Bolt Food exited Nigeria in 2023; the aggregators did not copy the owned-kitchen model.

market_need_then: Nigerian food delivery demand rose in the 2020 to 2021 lockdowns; the YC launch post reports 250,000 plus meals and $500K plus sales in about 11 months.

branding.name_origin: FoodCourt is the trade name; registered name Co-Kitchen Workspace Limited (CoKitchen); co-founder says there was never a rebrand, per TechCabal

identity.voice_and_tone: Short and upbeat: Good Food, Made Easy

branding.brand_signature: Portfolio of owned virtual restaurant brands under the FoodCourt app
branding.community_and_virality: TechCabal coverage of the dark kitchen model and customer surprise at the 2026 pause suggest customer awareness; no merch or fan evidence found

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in Nigerian tech press and by consumers with profitability claims in 2024, but generic name and dual naming (CoKitchen and FoodCourt) add confusion.

outcome_analysis: FoodCourt grew quickly from 2021 with owned virtual restaurants in Lagos and Abuja, raised a 2022 seed after YC S22, and reported profitability in 2024 per TechCabal. In 2026 unpaid salaries, a worker strike and vendor debts forced it to close its kitchens while a funding facility never arrived; it says it plans to relaunch, so the outcome is a pause rather than a confirmed shutdown.
notes: Seed amount conflicts: Seedtable and other aggregators say $500K (Sep 2022), Founderlodge says $3.4M (2022-11-29), TechCabal refers to a $1.7M 2022 round; amount left null. The YC directory claims over $28M funded, unverified. Directory status is Active but TechCabal reports operations paused in 2026 with the exit type left unknown. Investor list is from two aggregators (Seedtable, Extruct). Competitor sources are dated 2021 and Bolt official launch was October 2021.
